fun_highlights: The calling card (y_calling) genuinely gates four structurally different adult arcs — soldier, scholar, maker, wanderer — and each has its own vocation-specific cluster of three cards that fire at adult/midlife/elder stages, so the middle third of a life reads demonstrably differently depending on the choice made at 14-22. A soldier's midlife 3am ghost and a scholar's legacy dilemma are not the same card with different paint.

The callback system is the game's best mechanic from a choice-savorer's perspective. When cb_books_late fires at midlife because you chose 'keep it' at age 8, or when cb_outcast_return pays off the friend you sat beside in childhood, there is a genuine sense that the earlier decision had a real downstream shape. These moments earn their weight.

The era layer (war, plague, plenty, hard, turning) produces situational forks that only appear under specific era x vocation intersections — a soldier in wartime faces vx_soldier_war; a scholar in a turning age faces vx_scholar_turning. These cross-gates mean dynasty 8 in a plague era is structurally different from dynasty 3 in a fat-years era, not just tonally different.

The 'competing goods' cluster (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty) gives the choice-savorer what the genre promises: two-virtue dilemmas with no clearly correct answer. 'The thing you've always meant to do with your one life has come within reach — and taking it would ask real sacrifice of the people who depend on you' is a genuinely characterful fork.

The dynasty-memory cards (d_ancestor, d_motto_test) are a smart late-game mechanic: reading back who your house has become and asking whether you'll live up to it or step out from under it creates a real generational identity question that accumulates meaning over multiple dynasties.

Trait-gated cards (t_bookish, t_guarded, t_shrewd, t_stubborn, t_dreaming, t_restless) mean that the marked nature rolled at birth actually surfaces in at least one dedicated card per trait, so the child who was 'restless' faces a youth card the 'warm' child does not. This is genuine character-driven divergence.
staleness: The love/marriage/child spine is almost inescapable in shape even when the text varies. Across the 15 dynasties in the transcripts, the structural arc -- meet someone (y_love1 or a_meet_late) -> a_marry -> a_child -- lands in approximately 80% of lives. The engine nudges love at 0.30 per eligible draw; marriage at 0.55-0.62; child at 0.33-0.55. The result is that the domestic arc is the default life-shape and solitary/childless lives are rare exceptions (~20%). By dynasty 5-6, reading through another betrothal-marriage-child sequence in the transcript produces diminishing returns, even though the individual lines are different.

The a_marry card itself becomes a staleness source at high dynasties. The card's text rotates well, but the log line pattern is almost always 'Married [name]. [Short epigram].' across 15 dynasties. A choice_savorer notices that the marriage choice has exactly two options -- ask vs. not yet -- and the 'ask' outcome is narratively almost mandatory if you want a child. The fork is not characterful; it is structural bookkeeping.

The cb_corner/cb_reckless/cb_strayed callback loop recurs across dynasties 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13 in the transcripts. Because cut_a_corner and lived_reckless are easy flags to set (multiple paths to each), a very large fraction of lives end up triggering the same callbacks. By dynasty 8-10, seeing 'The corner Noor cut once, years ago...' is not fresh; it is the expected beat for any life that took a dishonest gain. The onceDyn cooldown of 3 generations does not prevent the same callback from landing in every 3rd or 4th life across a long session.

The e_bequest / succeed arc has the right idea but the actual choice (mind/means/heart/free) produces near-identical outcomes at the heir screen. The bequest is announced in a single line and the heir starts the same childhood card sequence regardless. A choice_savorer who has played 5+ dynasties has seen the heir-screen ritual enough times that the bequest choice feels perfunctory rather than meaningful across-generation leverage.

The 'a_work' promotion card and the 'a_small_lie / a_smallchoice' band-fillers read as filler by dynasty 4-5. They are structurally simple binary ethical forks that produce log lines without much downstream consequence. The work card in particular -- 'take the promotion (means up, bond down) vs. refuse (means down, spirit up)' -- is the same lever pulled multiple times in the same life (onceDyn flag doesn't apply), producing 'took the ladder over the table' / 'chose the table over the ladder' alternation without accumulation.

The x_reckoning (house reckoning) and s_great_burden / s_inheritance_dispute seat-gated cards are theoretically the most dynasty-layer-specific content, but in practice across the 15 dynasties they rarely fire in ways that visibly change the course of a life. The transcripts show only one reckoning (Dynasty 8, Roman Vane shielding himself), and it appears as a single log line without generating a memorable narrative thread. The dynasty mechanics feel underplayed as choice-driven content.

improvements.what: Add a second structural variant to a_marry: a 'propose and be refused' path that sets a distinct memory flag (proposed_refused) and gates a later callback at midlife or elder when the person encounters the love again after years apart. Currently the marriage fork is ask/defer -- the only real decision is timing. A refusal outcome would make the marriage moment genuinely branching rather than a yes-or-when question.
improvements.why: The marriage card is drawn in the majority of lives and its binary ask/not-yet fork is structurally weak for a choice-savorer. The ask option is almost always taken because not-taking it merely delays the same card. A refusal-and-reunion arc would create a distinct life-shape that does not currently exist in the domestic arc.

improvements.what: Reduce the base love-nudge probability from 0.30 to 0.15 and reduce the marriage safety-net from 0.62 to 0.45, while adding a genuine 'solitary life' track that has its own 3-card mini-arc (m_solitary already exists; extend it with a youth version and an elder flourishing card). The goal is to make roughly 35% of lives genuinely non-domestic in shape, not 20%.
improvements.why: The current nudge values mean that 'meet someone, marry, have a child' is the overwhelming default shape. The transcripts confirm this. For a choice-savorer, structural variety across life-shapes is the primary freshness driver; the current balance underweights non-domestic arcs.

improvements.what: Add a 'consequential refusal' mechanic to the vocation calling card: if a character born into a high-seat house (seat >= 4) refuses all four callings and drifts uncalled, gate a distinct 'inheritor who never chose' arc with 2-3 unique cards about wealth without purpose, identity without vocation. Currently the uncalled life simply has no vocation arc, which is a structural blank rather than a meaningful life-shape.
improvements.why: The calling card is the game's most consequential fork, and refusing it (which a curious choice_savorer will do) produces an empty downstream experience. Giving the uncalled life its own content would make refusal a genuine choice rather than an absence.

improvements.what: Gate the cb_corner callback behind a minimum number of decisions since the original cut_a_corner (e.g. at least 12 years and 3 decisions), and increase its onceDyn cooldown to 5 generations (from 3). Apply the same tightening to cb_reckless and cb_strayed. In the transcripts these three callbacks appear in 8 of 15 dynasties, making them the most visible staleness pattern in a long run.
improvements.why: Callbacks are the game's best mechanic -- they give earlier choices visible downstream weight -- but if they fire in every third life they become expected rather than surprising. Longer generational cooldowns and tighter eligibility would keep them feeling like earned payoffs rather than reliable beats.

improvements.what: Add one new card per vocation at the youth/young-adult stage (ages 18-30) that is specific to the vocation AND raises or lowers the house standing directly. Currently the vocation arcs gate adult content but do not interact with the dynasty layer until midlife at the earliest. A young maker opening a shop that succeeds or fails (affecting seat), or a young scholar publishing something that earns the house a scholarly reputation bump, would wire the vocation choice to the dynasty meter in the years immediately following the calling.
improvements.why: The calling and the dynasty meter are the two structural anchors of the game, but they operate largely independently until late midlife. Early cross-wiring would make the vocation choice feel like a dynasty decision as well as a personal one, deepening the cross-generational stakes for a choice_savorer.

verdict: A life offers more structural choice-variety than its meditative exterior suggests, but the domestic arc (meet/marry/child) is too dominant a template -- by dynasty 6-8 the transcripts reveal the same spine beneath different prose, and the most interesting non-domestic and cross-generational content is too rarely encountered to sustain a choice-savorer across a long session.
